questions.q: Why does this lesson say environment strategy needs to exist as a diagram, not just as one architect's informal understanding?
options: Because a diagram makes the strategy a shared, reviewable, onboarding-ready fact instead of institutional memory that disappears if that one architect leaves
Because Salesforce legally requires a diagram to be filed before any sandbox can be created
Because diagrams are purely decorative and have no practical function
Because written documentation is never allowed in Salesforce architecture
questions.explain: An environment diagram turns knowledge that otherwise lives only in one person's head into something a team can actually rely on, review, and hand off.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the five elements this lesson says a real environment diagram needs to show?
options: Every environment that exists, named consistently
The promotion path, with directional arrows showing which environment flows into which
Each environment's exact monthly dollar cost broken down by storage line item
Data posture -- whether an environment carries real, masked, or no data
questions.explain: The five elements this lesson names are: every environment, the promotion path, each environment's type/purpose, refresh relationships, and data posture -- a detailed cost breakdown by line item is not one of them.

questions.q: What does "data posture" mean as an element of an environment diagram?
options: The physical server location where an environment's data is hosted
How quickly a user can log into an environment
The total number of custom fields defined in an environment
Whether a given environment carries real data, masked data, or no data at all -- directly tied to the risk surface covered in Lessons 9 and 10
questions.explain: Data posture communicates exactly the risk surface this chapter's earlier lessons covered -- whether real sensitive data, masked data, or no data is present in each environment.

questions.q: Per this lesson, which role, besides the architect, is given as an example of someone who depends on an environment diagram, and why?
options: A marketing intern, because they need to know the company's social media schedule
A customer, because they need to see the diagram before making a purchase
A security reviewer, because the data-posture layer lets them assess real risk without having to interview the architect directly
No one besides the architect ever needs to reference this diagram
questions.explain: This lesson names a new developer (to know where to start), a release manager (to know the correct promotion order), and a security reviewer (to assess data-posture risk directly) as people who rely on this artifact.

questions.q: How does this lesson say Chapter 3's two case studies relate to the content of this lesson?
options: They are unrelated -- Chapter 3 covers entirely new material with no connection to environment diagrams
Chapter 3 replaces diagramming with a purely verbal description method instead
Chapter 3 only applies to organizations that have never created a sandbox
They are, underneath everything else, exercises in producing exactly this kind of diagram for two very different organizational scales
questions.explain: This lesson explicitly frames the upcoming small-team and enterprise case studies as applications of the same diagramming skill, just at two different organizational scales.
